subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers close, adopt, or replace the linked conflicting fork PR before this issue gets a new narrow fix PR?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the issue is already linked to an open conflicting fork PR with closing syntax; ClawSweeper should not queue a competing fix until maintainers decide what to do with that candidate.

options.title: Replace the linked fork PR
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork PR and queue a narrow replacement against the active Telegram native approval runtime, preserving contributor credit where appropriate.

options.title: Ask the fork author to update
options.body: Keep the linked fork PR as the landing path and ask the author to retarget the active runtime seam with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt the closed runtime approach manually
options.body: Use the closed same-repo runtime PR as implementation reference, but land it through a fresh maintainer-owned branch rather than reopening stale PR state.

recommendation.title: Replace the linked fork PR
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork PR and queue a narrow replacement against the active Telegram native approval runtime, preserving contributor credit where appropriate.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the centralized native approval lifecycle and are the strongest history signal for the approval runtime owner boundary.
